notes: Keypad mode: the pad offers an unexplained "and" key as the mixed-number separator with no hint that "2 and 1/2" is the expected form, and the explanation's own "5/2" phrasing is a form a child would plausibly type instead. The ruler and bar are drawn small relative to the empty space above them.
The minute hand is drawn long enough that its tip covers the "6" numeral on the face; the explanation also says "The hour hand is at 6" when the hand is rendered halfway between 6 and 7.
Explanation says "The minute hand is at 0 (0 minutes)" though the face is labelled 12, and "The hour hand is past 7" when it sits exactly on 7; the minute hand tip also draws over the "12".

Distractors 7:32/7:33/7:34 sit one minute tick apart on a ~200 px clock face, so choosing between them is a pixel-perception test rather than a clock-reading one, and the explanation is just "It is 7:33." with no method for counting the ticks.
Explanation card ends with a doubled period: "at night" tells you it is p.m..
datasetPool is 200, so this single generator sample is not representative of the concept; the sampled item (clock showing the 7:45 start time, stepwise explanation) was clean.

The coin disc is printed with "1¢", so the answer is read off the label instead of identifying the coin, which defeats the concept; the explanation also reads "A penny is worth 1 cents" and "0" is an implausible distractor for a coin value.
Explanation reads "1 feet = 12 inches." — the unit name is not singularised.
